newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banking rationalisation gaining momentum-S&P.
newsitem.headline: Japan banking rationalisation gaining momentum-S&P.

text.p: The restructuring plans recently announced by two big Japanese banks could be a sign that the rationalisation of Japan's financial sector was gaining momentum, Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday.
On April 1, Nippon Credit Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, both among the nation's top 20 banks, announced restructuring steps that included a withdrawal from overseas operations.
Hokkaido Takushoku also said that it would merge with a regional bank, Hokkaido Bank Ltd, on April 1, 1998.
"Standard & Poor's views as a default NCB's request that domestic holders of its subordinated debt accept a conversion to equity," the rating agency said in a statement.
Further, it said that NCB's move to let three non-bank financial affiliates go bankrupt had raised worries that other major financial institutions may follow suit.

"The rating agency had already factored into its ratings of Japanese banks the possibility of less government protection over time, placing more emphasis on the stand-alone financial strength of each institution," S&P said.

It also said that the recent announcement by the Fair Trade Commission, Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog, that it would give financial institutions more leeway to merge was an indication that the Japanese government was preparing for further consolidation in the banking sector.
